entries.name: One Button Dialog Function
entries.description: Displays a dialog box that contains a message and a single button.

terminals.name: message
terminals.description: message is the text to display in the dialog box. The dialog box expands when you add more text. This function automatically wraps the text based on the size of the dialog box. The dialog box can display as much text as your computer screen can display. If you want a scrollbar to show when the size of the dialog box exceeds your desired size, use the Three Button Dialog VI. With this VI, you can convert a three button dialog box to a one or two button dialog box by wiring an empty string to a button text input to hide that button.

terminals.name: button name ("OK")
terminals.description: button name is the name displayed in the dialog box button. The default is OK .

terminals.name: true
terminals.description: true returns a value of TRUE when this dialog box closes, regardless of whether you close the dialog by using the dialog box button or by using the close window button. You may use this output to provide execution ordering control for downstream functions.

entries.name: Two Button Dialog Function
entries.description: Displays a dialog box that contains a message and two buttons.

terminals.name: message

With this VI, you can convert a three button dialog box to a one or two button dialog box by wiring an empty string to a button text input to hide that button.

terminals.name: T button name ("OK")
terminals.description: T button name is the name displayed on one of the dialog box buttons. The default is OK .

terminals.name: F button name ("Cancel")
terminals.description: F button name is the name displayed on one of the dialog box buttons. The default is Cancel .

terminals.name: T button?
terminals.description: T button? returns a value of TRUE if you click the dialog box button named T button name . If you click the dialog box button named F button name or click the close window button, T button? returns a value of FALSE.

entries.name: Three Button Dialog
entries.description: Displays a dialog box that contains a message and three buttons.

terminals.name: Justify Message (Left)
terminals.description: Justify Message sets the justification of the text that is displayed.

terminals.name: Window Title ("")
terminals.description: Window Title is the text to display in the title bar of the dialog box.

terminals.name: message
terminals.description: message is the text to display in the dialog box. The dialog box has a maximum size based on your computer screen resolution and system font size. If the text exceeds the maximum size of the dialog box, a vertical scrollbar appears on the right side. Scroll to display the text beyond the maximum size.

terminals.name: Left Button Text ("Yes")
terminals.description: Left Button Text is the text to display on the left button. The default is Yes .

terminals.name: Center Button Text ("No")
terminals.description: Center Button Text is the text to display on the center button. The default is No .

terminals.name: Right Button Text ("Cancel")
terminals.description: Right Button Text is the text to display on the right button. The default is Cancel .

terminals.name: Keyboard Shortcuts (Left is <Enter>)
terminals.description: Keyboard Shortcuts specifies keyboard shortcuts for each button in the dialog box.

terminals.name: Shift
terminals.description: If Shift is TRUE, the keyboard shortcut includes the <Shift> key.

terminals.name: Key
terminals.description: Key is the name of the shortcut key.

terminals.name: Center Button Key Shortcut
terminals.description: Center Button Key Shortcut specifies a keyboard shortcut for the center button.

terminals.name: Shift
terminals.description: If Shift is TRUE, the keyboard shortcut includes the <Shift> key.

terminals.name: Key
terminals.description: Key is the name of the shortcut key.

terminals.name: Right Button Key Shortcut
terminals.description: Right Button Key Shortcut specifies a keyboard shortcut for the right button.

terminals.description: If Shift is TRUE, the keyboard shortcut includes the <Shift> key.

terminals.name: Key
terminals.description: Key is the name of the shortcut key.

terminals.name: Allow user to close window? (TRUE)
terminals.description: If Allow user to close window? is TRUE (default), the operating system window close button appears in the dialog box, and the user can close the dialog box without clicking the left, center, or right buttons.

terminals.name: Which Button?
terminals.description: Which Button? indicates which button the user clicked.

entries.name: Wait For Front Panel Activity Function
entries.description: Pauses the execution of the calling VI block diagram in run mode until the function detects front panel activity in the front panel you want to monitor.

terminals.description: If do not wait! is TRUE, the VI runs without pausing execution.

terminals.description: front panel is a reference to the VI you want to monitor for front panel activity. You can wire a VI, front panel, or control reference to this input. If you wire a control reference, the function monitors the activity of the front panel containing the control. If you do not specify a reference, the function monitors the front panel activity of the VI in which you place the function. You must wire a reference to a VI or object in a local application instance . You cannot wire a reference to a VI or object in a remote application instance.

terminals.name: timeout ms (-1 never timeout)

entries.name: Flush Event Queue Function
entries.description: Discards the least recent notify events from one or more event queues. If the event queue that you want to discard includes filter events, this function stops at the first filter event in the queue and discards only the events that occurred previous to the stop.

terminals.name: oldest event time
terminals.description: oldest event time is the event timestamp, in milliseconds, when you want to start keeping events. This function discards all events previous to the event time you specify. This millisecond timer can accept the value returned by the Tick Count (ms) function.

terminals.name: event registration refnum
terminals.description: event registration refnum is a reference to an event registration refnum associated with the queue you want to flush. You can also wire a cluster of event registration refnums to flush more than one queue. This input is required unless the Flush Event Queue function is in an event case of an Event structure, in which case it will flush the enclosing Event structure's static event queue. If this input is wired, the Flush Event Queue function is in an event case of an Event structure, and include static events? is unwired or True, the function will flush both the dynamic event queue(s) associated with the wired refnum(s) and the Event structure's static queue.

terminals.name: include static events? (T)
terminals.description: include static events? specifies whether you want to include the enqueued static events associated with an Event structure in the flush operation. The default is TRUE if you place the Flush Event Queue function in an event case of an Event structure. Otherwise, the default is FALSE. Note If you wire include static events? , you must place this function inside the Event structure that handles the static events you want to include or omit from the flush operation.

terminals.name: event type or object
terminals.description: event type or object specifies which notify events you want to discard within the criteria set by oldest event time and keep most recent . Refer to the Details section for more information about how to specify which events you want to discard.

terminals.name: error in (no error)
terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

terminals.name: keep most recent
terminals.description: keep most recent specifies the number of most recent events to keep in the event queue. If you wire the event type or object parameter, keep most recent affects only the events of the type you specify. If you flush more than one event queue, keep most recent includes the total number of events to keep from all specified event queues. Note If you leave both oldest event time and keep most recent unwired, the function discards all events in all queues that meet any criteria set by event type or object . If you wire both oldest event time and keep most recent , this function keeps all events starting at the event time you specify and all events within the number of most recent events you specify.

terminals.name: event reg refnum out
terminals.description: event reg refnum out returns the event registration refnum associated with the flushed event queue.

terminals.name: number of events discarded

entries.name: Insert Menu Items Function
entries.description: Inserts menu items specified by item names or item tags into a menu or a submenu within the menu. (Real-Time Module) You cannot use this function in VIs that run on RT targets.

terminals.name: menu tag
terminals.description: menu tag specifies the submenu in which to insert the items. If you do not specify menu tag , the function inserts the items at the top level of the menu.

terminals.name: menu reference
terminals.description: menu reference is the reference to a menu bar in a VI or to a shortcut menu of a control. You can obtain this refnum with the Current VI's Menubar function or with the MenuRef event data field of menu events.

terminals.name: item names
terminals.description: item names identifies the items to insert in the menu. item names is the string that appears in the menu. You can wire either item names or item tags , in which case both names and tags have the same values. If you want to insert only one item, wire a string to item names .

terminals.name: item tags
terminals.description: item tags identifies the items to insert in the menu. item tags is the string that is returned if the menu item is selected. You can wire either item names or item tags , in which case both names and tags have the same values. If you want to insert only one item, wire a string to item tags . Use application item tags to insert application menu items.

terminals.name: error in (no error)
terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

terminals.name: after item
terminals.description: after item specifies the position where the items are inserted. after item can be a tag (string) of an existing item or a position index (zero based integer) in the menu. To insert at the beginning of the menu, wire a number less than 0 to after item . To insert at the end of the menu, wire a number larger than the number of items in the menu. You can insert application items using application tags . You can insert a separator using the application tag APP_SEPARATOR . The function always ensures that the tags of all the inserted menu items are unique to the menu hierarchy by appending numbers to the supplied tags, if necessary.

terminals.name: menu reference out
terminals.description: menu reference out returns menu reference unchanged.

terminals.name: item tags out
terminals.description: item tags out returns the actual tags of the inserted items. If the function does not find menu tag or after item (tag), the function returns an error.

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

entries.name: Delete Menu Items Function
entries.description: Deletes menu items from the menu or a submenu within the menu. (Real-Time Module) You cannot use this function in VIs that run on RT targets.

terminals.name: menu reference
terminals.description: menu reference is the reference to a menu bar in a VI or to a shortcut menu of a control. You can obtain this refnum with the Current VI's Menubar function or with the MenuRef event data field of menu events.

terminals.name: menu tag
terminals.description: menu tag specifies the submenu from which to delete items. If you do not specify menu tag , the function deletes all items from the menu.

terminals.name: items
terminals.description: items can be a tag (string) of an existing item, an array of tags of existing items, a position index (zero-based integer) of an item in the menu, or an array of position indexes of items in the menu. The default is to delete all the items in the menu or submenu specified by menu tag . If any of the specified items have a submenu, the function deletes the submenu and all its contents. Use application item tags for menus or shortcut menus to delete application menu items. Because separators do not have unique tags, you can delete them using their positional indexes.

entries.name: Control Online Help Function
entries.description: Controls a compiled help file by displaying the table of contents, jumping to a specific topic in the file, or closing the help file. You can create a compiled help file and use this function to link from a VI to the help file. You also can use this function to display an HTML file in the default browser. (Real-Time Module) You cannot use this function in VIs that run on RT targets.

terminals.name: Operation
terminals.description: Operation is the operation to perform on the help file. 0 Contents —Displays the table of contents of the help file. If you use this function to control a .chm file, setting this input to 0 displays the table of contents, index, or search tab, depending on which tab was visible the last time you closed the .chm file. 1 Key —Displays a specific topic in the help file using a keyword in the help file index or using the name of an individual HTML file in the compiled help file. 2 Close —Closes the help file.

terminals.name: String to search for
terminals.description: String to search for is the index keyword or HTML filename for the topic in the help file that you want to display. The default is an empty string. LabVIEW ignores this string if Operation is 0 or 2. If this string contains an index keyword, the string must match the index keyword as it appears in the help file index. To jump to a topic with a multi-level index keyword, enter the first-level index keyword, a colon, and the second-level index keyword. Do not separate the elements with spaces. For example, a error codes:GPIB string jumps to a topic with a first-level index keyword of error codes and a second-level index keyword of GPIB . If Path to the help file contains a path to an HTML Help ( .chm ) file, this string can contain the filename ( .htm or .html ) of an individual HTML file in the HTML Help project.

terminals.name: Path to the help file
terminals.description: Path to the help file is the path or symbolic path to the compiled help file you want to control. The help file can have a .chm or .hlp extension. (macOS and Linux) If this input contains a path to a .chm file and the file does not exist, LabVIEW ignores this input. However, if String to search for contains an HTML filename and that HTML file is in the help\html\ help .chm directory where help .chm is the filename you wire to this input, LabVIEW displays that HTML file in the default browser. If this input contains a path to a .chm file and String to search for contains an index keyword, this function does not display an HTML file.
